items.title: Caufield scores OT winner as Canadiens come back to beat Mammoth
items.body: Cole Caufield scored the winner 30 seconds into overtime as the Montreal Canadiens overcame Logan Cooley’s hat trick to beat the Utah Mammoth 5-4 in an action-packed affair Thursday night. Captain Nick Suzuki had a goal and two assists in his return from a six-game absence for Montreal (10-3-3). Adam Engstrom added his first career goal, while Kirby Dach and Arber Xhekaj also scored. Jakub Dobes made 16 saves two nights after the Canadiens made some unwanted history. Montreal lost 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday after blowing a 4-0 lead with 2:39 remaining in regulation, marking the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. Cooley scored his second hat trick of the season and added an assist while Nick Schmaltz had a goal and two helpers for Utah (10-6-1). Sebastian Cossa stopped 30 shots. Dach tied the game 3-3 with a power-play goal 69 seconds into the third period, jamming in a loose puck in the crease. The Mammoth regained the lead at 7:14 when Schmaltz scored on the power play, but Montreal evened things again when Engstrom beat Cossa with a wrist shot at 14:54. After Tuesday’s collapse, Thursday’s start wasn’t much better for the Canadiens. Cooley opened the scoring on Utah’s first shot at 1:42 of the first period, beating Engstrom to the outside before cruising through the crease and tucking a backhand around Dobes. The speedy forward scored his second on the power play at 9:24 — albeit on a questionable tripping call against Josh Anderson — when he slipped behind defenceman Alexandre Carrier, took a heads-up stretch pass from Schmaltz and beat Dobes five-hole. items.title: Mammoth’s Cooley becomes fastest active player to five career hat tricks
items.summary: Cooley scored his fifth career hat trick faster than Alex Ovechkin did, doing so by two games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images It’s not every day that a player reaches a goal-scoring mark faster than the GR8. During a game against the Montreal Canadiens on Thursday night, Utah Mammoth forward Logan Cooley scored a hat trick, the fifth of his young NHL career. The 22-year-old accomplished the feat in just his 228th game, making him the fastest active player to register five three-goal performances. Cooley even beat the great Alex Ovechkin, as he potted his fifth hat trick two games faster than the Washington Capitals captain. Cooley found the back of the net twice before the halfway mark of the first period in the Bell Centre, giving the Mammoth an early lead. After the Canadiens came back to tie the game, the former Minnesota Golden Gopher put Utah back out in front once again just past the halfway mark of the middle frame. It was Cooley’s second hat trick in four games, as he notched a trio of goals in an overtime win against the Pittsburgh Penguins last Thursday. He added an assist in Montreal to give him a four-point night. Unfortunately for Cooley, the Canadiens got the last laugh, as Cole Caufield capped off a late comeback for the home team, scoring in overtime to give Montreal a 5-4 win. The Pittsburgh native scored his first hat trick back in his rookie season in 2023-24, when the franchise was known as the Arizona Coyotes. After not putting together a hat trick in his sophomore campaign, Cooley posted two three-goal nights last season. With his impressive outing against the Habs, Cooley now has 11 goals in the 2026-27 season, tying Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews for fifth in the NHL in goals. items.title: Zacha scores twice to lead Bruins to victory over struggling Penguins
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Pavel Zacha scored twice and the Boston Bruins beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-2 on Thursday night. Morgan Geekie scored in his third straight game and had an assist. Elias Lindholm, Mark Kastelic and Fraser Minten also scored for the Bruins, who have won three straight. Boston has won 10 of its last 13 games overall. David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka added two assists and Michael DiPietro stopped 16 shots for the Bruins, who snapped a three-game road losing streak. Boston has points in its last seven trips to Pittsburgh, dating to Nov. 1, 2022. Justin Brazeau scored his first goal in his second game of the season since returning from a training camp injury. Nick Robertson also scored for the Penguins, who struggled defensively against the Bruins. Pittsburgh captain Sidney Crosby did not record a point and remains tied with Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time scoring list with 1,771 points. Arturs Silovs made 18 saves for the Penguins, who lost their fourth straight. Pittsburgh has dropped eight of its last 10 games overall. Boston led 3-1 after the first period and 5-2 through 40 minutes. Zacha scored both of his goals on a 2-on-1, as did Minten. Geekie scored on a partial breakaway after a poor Pittsburgh line change, and Lindholm found the back of the net following an Erik Karlsson turnover in his own zone. Karlsson was a minus-4 for Pittsburgh. Bruins: Open a four-game homestand Sunday against Florida. Boston plays 10 of its next 11 games at home. Penguins: Begin a three-game West Coast trip Saturday at Los Angeles.

items.title: Bouchard becomes fastest defenceman in Oilers history to hit 10 goals
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers are off to a hot start to the season, and key players just keep breaking records. On Thursday night, it was Evan Bouchard 's turn as the defenceman became the fastest blue-liner in Oilers history to hit 10 goals, reaching the mark in 17 games. Bouchard's double-digit marker came late in the first period against the Anaheim Ducks on a power play to tie the game. He broke a record previously held by Paul Coffey, who hit 10 goals in 22 games back in 1983-84. The 27-year-old defenceman has been prolific to start the year, with 10 goals and 29 points, ranking third in league scoring. With an assist on the Bouchard goal, captain Connor McDavid also extended his assist streak to 17 games. The Oilers are first in the Pacific Division with an 11-2-3 record.

items.title: Oilers’ Podkolzin receives game misconduct vs. Ducks
items.body: Vasily Podkolzin came to his captain's defence on Thursday, but ended up with a game misconduct for his efforts. Podkolzin was ejected from the Edmonton Oilers ' game against the Anaheim Ducks midway through the first period. He received the misconduct for fighting Drew Helleson, who had checked Connor McDavid into the Anaheim net. The play came with just under 12 minutes remaining in the period as McDavid drove to the Ducks crease before Helleson bumped the Oilers captain into the post. McDavid stayed down on the ice as players from both teams converged. Podkolzin then found Helleson in the scrum, starting the fight. The 25-year-old winger was then assessed a two-minute instigator and five-minute fighting major to go along with the misconduct. McDavid eventually went down the tunnel, but did return to the game. Cutter Gauthier went on to score the game's opening goal on Anaheim's ensuing five-minute power play.

Both forwards have been out since the opening weekend of the season. Kasper is the more significant of the two. Appleton, 30, offers bottom-six depth and landed on injured reserve after the season’s second game. items.body: New Jersey native, former US Marine Bob Walsh drops puck at Prudential Center NEWARK, N.J. -- Bob Walsh has experienced events far more daunting than dropping a puck in front of thousands of hockey fans. But the 100-year-old World War II veteran could hardly hide his excitement about receiving that honor at Prudential Center on Thursday. The Far Hills, New Jersey native was recognized by the New Jersey Devils as part of Military Appreciation Night before their game against the St. Louis Blues. "It's a real treat, I'll tell you that," Walsh told NHL.com. "I'm going to drop the puck and that's unbelievable. I never expected anything like that." Walsh enlisted in the United States Marine Corps in 1943 and was assigned to the 2nd Marine Division. His service took him to Okinawa, Japan, where American forces began one of the Pacific campaign's bloodiest battles on April 1, 1945. Asked what inspired him to join the Marines, Walsh offered a lighthearted explanation. "I tell everybody John Wayne movies," he said with a grin. "A friend of mine joined the Marines a year ahead of me, so I thought that was pretty cool. We didn't do it together, but we ended up together, somehow." Walsh said serving at Okinawa remains one of the proudest moments of his military career. The experience also left him with lessons that have endured for more than eight decades. "Being faithful to everything and treating your people with good faith and respect," Walsh said. Walsh was once an avid hockey fan, though he joked that following the game has become slightly more challenging. "I was a real hockey fan years ago," he said. The most recent win came Tuesday in Pittsburgh, where Hertl scored his second power-play goal of the night in the final minute of regulation for a 3-2 victory. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images The New York Islanders have agreed to terms on a one-year contract with defenseman Ben Hutton, the club announced Thursday evening. Hutton, 33, had signed a professional tryout agreement with the Islanders on Monday. According to PuckPedia , his new contract with the Islanders is a one-way NHL deal that carries a pro-rated $900,000 cap hit. The Vancouver Canucks originally selected Hutton in the fifth round (No. 147 overall) of the 2012 NHL Draft. The Brockville, Ont. product spent his first three post-draft seasons at the University of Maine before turning pro in 2015. Hutton immediately established himself as an NHL regular with the Canucks in the 2015-16 season, and save for four games with the Utica Comets directly out of school, he has never played in the AHL during his professional career. Hutton followed up his first four NHL seasons in Vancouver with a single-season stint with the Los Angeles Kings ; following that, he split the 2020-21 campaign between the Anaheim Ducks and Toronto Maple Leafs before joining the Golden Knights. items.body: Wore lavender mullet, brought smiles to patients shooting puck from left circle ARLINGTON, Va. -- Alex Ovechkin 's office was open for visitors during the Washington Capitals' annual Hockey Fights Cancer skate at MedStar Capitals Iceplex on Thursday. Having the opportunity to shoot the puck with the NHL's all-time goal-scoring leader from his favorite spot in the left circle brought plenty of smiles from children impacted by cancer who participated in the skate with Capitals players. "To see how they smile, to see how they have fun, score goals, skate around, chat with us, it's very important and it's very cool," Ovechkin said. For the skate, each player was paired with a child from Blood Cancer United Mid-Atlantic, Make-A-Wish Mid-Atlantic, MedStar Health or Sunrise Day Camp Greater Washington. This year's skate was different, though, after Ovechkin, who holds the NHL record with 930 goals, announced Oct. 5 that this will be his final season in the League. So, instead of being paired with one child, the 41-year-old forward set up shop in the "Ovi's Office" station in the left circle, and each child took turns shooting from there. "The kids have fun," Ovechkin said. "They shoot the pucks. They (skate) around, smiling, laughing and their parents are happy, so it's very important." Ovechkin appeared to enjoy it as much as the children. Like some of them, their parents and his teammates, Ovechkin donned a lavender mullet wig to join the fun. "He's always got the biggest smile out there and has a great time," Capitals coach Spencer Carbery said. "I bet if you ask him in a few years … he'll miss days like this, being able to give back like this." items.title: Rangers put goalie James Reimer on waivers after one start
items.body: James Reimer ’s time with the New York Rangers appears to be coming to an end after making just one start that lasted one period. The Rangers put Reimer on waivers Thursday and could send him to Hartford of the American Hockey League if he is not claimed by one of the NHL’s other 31 clubs. Reimer was pulled after allowing three goals on eight shots in 20 minutes on the way to a home loss to Los Angeles on Oct. 26. New York late last month signed him to a contract for this season in the hopes that the 38-year-old could spell Dylan Garand, who had been playing almost nonstop since franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season with a knee injury. Instead, Reimer struggled in his only chance, and Garand has played in 11 consecutive games. After posting a 1.85 goals-against average and .929 save percentage in his first six games, Garand is at 3.50 and .877 in his past five. Reimer going on waivers now seems to indicate Joonas Korpisalo is nearing a return from his lower-body injury. Korpisalo stopped 34 of the 37 shots he faced in a minor league rehab start with Hartford on Wednesday night. It was Korpisalo's injury during the first week of the season that set this goalie carousel in motion. The Rangers acquired him from Boston over the summer to back up Shesterkin, and Garand cleared waivers prior to opening night to go to the AHL's Wolf Pack and play regularly. Garand was recalled when Korpisalo got hurt and became the go-to option when Shesterkin went down.

items.title: Rangers waive James Reimer, place Sean Durzi on injured reserve
items.summary: Reimer will dress on Thursday night, as Joonas Korpisalo is set to return to the lineup.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Some roster moves on Broadway as an Original Six team prepares for an upcoming road trip. On Thursday, the New York Rangers placed goaltender James Reimer on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. The team also put defenseman Sean Durzi on injured reserve. If Reimer clears waivers on Friday, he’ll be eligible to return to the Rangers’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack. He’s expected to back up Dylan Garand in Thursday night’s game against the Philadelphia Flyers , but with Joonas Korpisalo nearing a return to the lineup, the Rangers need to make room on their roster. Reimer signed a one-year contract with the Rangers last month, giving the team some depth at goaltending amid injury woes to Korpisalo and Igor Shesterkin . He’s dressed in four games, only making one start. That came last Monday, when he gave up three goals on eight shots against the Los Angeles Kings before being pulled after the first period. The 38-year-old’s cap hit is a prorated $850,000. He has already played one game for the Wolf Pack, a 35-save shutout against the Providence Bruins on Oct. 23. Durzi’s placement on IR is retroactive to Oct. 26, when he was in the lineup in a 6-3 loss to the Los Angeles Kings. He’s been plagued with an undisclosed injury that has forced him to miss the past two games, with the Rangers expecting the 28-year-old to miss even more time, as he’s not going to be joining the team on its upcoming four-game road trip through the Pacific Division, which begin on Saturday with a matchup against the Seattle Kraken . In 14 games this season, the Mississauga, Ont. native has scored two goals and five points, with a plus/minus of -1 while averaging 19:52 of ice time per game.

items.body: The Calgary Flames activated goaltender Devin Cooley from injured reserve on Thursday, Sportsnet's Eric Francis reported. Arsenii Sergeev was assigned to the AHL's Calgary Wranglers in a corresponding move. Cooley has been out since he suffered a lower-body injury on Oct. 28 in a game against the Edmonton Oilers. Oilers forward Colton Dach crashed into Cooley with 12 seconds remaining in the opening 20 minutes and received a two-minute penalty for goaltender interference. Cooley remained in for the final 12 seconds but was not on the bench to start the second. He was then ruled out for the remainder of the game with a lower-body injury. The 29-year-old had been red-hot before he went down injured, allowing just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four starts. With Cooley out, Dustin Wolf started three of four games, picking up two wins. Cooley's first chance to return to the net will be on Friday when the Flames host the Anaheim Ducks.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Photo from Anders Marshall/Euro The Court of Arbitration for Sport released a public statement on Thursday afternoon, saying the International Ice Hockey Federation “did not present sufficient evidence to establish the legal requirements for the non-participation of Russian teams.” The CAS recently ruled that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation would be allowed to enter teams in IIHF events, such as the upcoming World Junior Championship in Alberta. Russia has been banned from IIHF competition since the nation invaded Ukraine shortly after the 2022 Beijing Olympics, which saw Russian athletes play under the ‘Russian Olympic Committee’ banner. The country was banned along with Belarus, which supported Russia during the war. According to the organization, both the RIHF and the IIHF submitted their disputes with the CAS to help solve the issue, with the CAS publishing their decision on Oct. 30. “The CAS Panel noted that the organisational consequences of this ruling, as well as the potential introduction of a neutrality regime, which are now at the centre of public debate, were neither substantiated by sufficient evidence nor sought by the IIHF during the proceedings. CAS cannot impose measures that have not been requested by the Parties,” Thursday’s CAS statement read. Multiple nations have already announced they would boycott playing against Russia in tournament competition, with multiple sponsors also threatening to pull out if action isn’t taken. The IIHF itself previously said they were disappointed in the decision from the CAS. items.title: Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki returning to lineup vs. Mammoth
items.body: Montreal captain Nick Suzuki will return to the lineup Thursday night against the Utah Mammoth as the Canadiens look to rebound from Tuesday's historic loss to the Winnipeg Jets. Suzuki was ruled out for two to four weeks after defenceman Michael Kesselring's shot struck his left hand in the third period of Montreal's 2-1 loss to the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 20. The 27-year-old centre missed his first six contests after playing in 546 consecutive regular-season games to begin his career. The Canadiens (9-3-3) managed well without their captain, winning five straight games before falling 5-4 in overtime to the Jets in an epic collapse. Winnipeg rallied from 4-0 down with 2:39 remaining in regulation, making for the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. Jakub Dobes will get the start as Montreal looks to respond against the visiting Mammoth (10-6-0). Suzuki will rejoin wingers Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovsky on the Canadiens' first line. After producing 101 points in 2025-26 — and winning the Selke Trophy as the league's best defensive forward — the London, Ont., native has five goals and seven assists through 12 games this season. Ivan Demidov remains out with a lower-body injury despite reaching the end of his two-to-four-week recovery timeline. The 20-year-old winger, who led all rookies in points with 62 last season, hasn't played since the Canadiens' second game on Oct. 3.

items.title: Mandated neck protection, high-sticking pucks permitted for 2026-27 PWHL season
items.summary: Among changes for Year 4, players can play the puck above their shoulders this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sarah Boeke/PWHL Ahead of its fourth season of operation, the Professional Women’s Hockey League is making some changes to its rulebook. On Thursday, the league announced a few tweaks ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, including clarifications on body checking, mandated neck protection, new high-sticking rules, and some experimentation with overtime during the preseason. Neck guards have been a point of contention around the game ever since Adam Johnson’s tragic passing in 2023 . Since then, the IIHF , USA Hockey , American Hockey League and the NHL have mandated the use of neck guards for their athletes. Now, the PWHL is requiring all players and goaltenders to wear cut-resistant neck protection during games, including pregame warmups. An interesting rule being implemented this year is that players can now knock the puck out of the air with their stick above the shoulders. Unlike previous years, the play is blown dead after the puck is knocked down by a player and either that player or their teammate touches the puck. Now, play can continue, regardless of who bats the puck out of the air. Also, players can score when deflecting the puck high in the air, eliminating the judgment call from on- and off-ice officials about whether a player’s stick was above the crossbar. A similar rule was adopted by the WCHA prior to the 2025-26 season. One point in the rule is that players can cradle the puck above their shoulders (a la the Michigan goal). However, if a player tries to cradle the puck on a penalty shot or shootout, the play will be blown dead and the shot will be complete. Body checking has been a welcome addition to the women’s game. items.body: Register Login Arturs Silovs Is Now The Penguins’ Starter By Josh Cybulski | at November 5, 2026 10:00 am A quick glance at Arturs Silovs ’ numbers might make you think he was an average-to-below-average goaltender during his brief tenure with the Penguins, but a deeper dive tells a different story. Silovs wasn’t great last year, posting below-average numbers in many statistical categories, with an .888 SV% and a 3.07 GAA in 39 games. This season, his traditional metrics are slightly better, with a 2.98 GAA and an .889 SV% in nine games, but his underlying numbers are much better. According to MoneyPuck , Silovs’ goals saved above expected last year were -11.9, while this year he is +2.5. That improvement is also quite obvious when you watch him play, as the Penguins give up a ton of high-danger chances, and Silovs has kept them in quite a few games this season. Entering this year, Sergei Murashov was expected to become the starter at some point, but given the start he’s had this season, Silovs is going to have some say in how that plays out and could be the starter as the season wears on. The Penguins acquired Silovs from the Vancouver Canucks for a song (a 2027 fourth-round pick and Chase Stillman) during the summer of 2025. items.summary: Pettersson is producing at a point-per-game pace for the first time since his contract extension, but is it legit?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources No player better represents the potential – and ultimate disappointment – of the Vancouver Canucks ‘ previous core of players better than Elias Pettersson. Sure, Quinn Hughes was the face of it, and his jumping ship to the Minnesota Wild triggered the Canucks’ current rebuild. But at the same time, the only wasted potential Hughes had in Vancouver was minimal playoff success. He rose to superstardom as one of the league’s top defensemen with the Canucks, won a Norris Trophy in 2024 and was still at the top of his game when he was traded, ensuring Vancouver received solid assets in return for him. Pettersson best represents the “what if” of this era for the Canucks because he himself has become a “what if.” He broke out onto the scene with an electric rookie season in 2018-19, accumulating 28 goals and 66 points in 71 games, and captured the Calder Memorial Trophy for his efforts. He followed that up with another 66-point season in 2019-20 (this time in 68 games), but impressed come playoff time with seven goals and 18 points in 17 games as the Canucks came two goals (not counting two empty net goals) shy of a Western Conference Final appearance. items.title: Winnipeg Jets recall forward Brayden Yager from AHL
items.body: Forward Brayden Yager has been recalled from the AHL, the team announced on Thursday. Yager, 22, has made one NHL appearance this season, logging 14 minutes, one shot and one face-off win in an overtime loss to the Dallas Stars on Oct. 22. The 14th-overall pick in 2023 has played a total of four NHL games, the first three coming last season, but has yet to register a point with the Jets. He was drafted by the Pittsburgh Penguins and was later traded to Winnipeg in 2024. Yager has spent most of the 2026-27 campaign with the Manitoba Moose, racking up seven goals and five assists in 10 games. The Saskatchewan native played 68 games for the AHL club last season and posted 10 goals and 20 assists. He'll look to help the Jets build momentum as they enter Thursday on the heels of a historic comeback OT win over the Montreal Canadiens that snapped a nine-game winless skid.

items.title: Sharks’ Sherwood calls Kings ‘disrespectful,’ demands his teammates ‘do something about it’
items.summary: Adrian Kempe had a hat trick and Quinton Byfield scored twice as the Kings defeated the Sharks Wednesday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Griffin Hooper San Jose Sharks’ forward Kiefer Sherwood said his team was “disrespected” by the Los Angeles Kings during the Sharks’ 7-2 loss Wednesday night. Sherwood, who finished the night with two shots and 17:39 of ice time, “They were up 6-2, put their top power play out, (Kings’ forward Artemi) Panarin is blocking shots, celebrating to his bench. It’s disrespectful. Until we do something about it, things aren’t going to change unless we man up and do something about it.” Sherwood, now with two goals and eight points in 17 games this season, also said him and his teammates had just held a players-only meeting after the game. “We’re going to move forward here and we got a lot to learn,” he said. “Listen, it’s better to go through the growing pains now than later on, right? We’re going to stick together and get through it together, and we’re going to fix our mindset and our work ethic for the next game, and we’re going to get gritty.” “This one obviously sucks, but no one’s feeling sorry for themselves,” Sherwood added. “Until we do something about it, stuff’s not going to change.” The Sharks are now 7-9-1 with 15 points and losses in five of their last six games and seven of their last 10. Captain Macklin Celebrini, now in his third NHL season, leads the team in all offensive categories with six goals and 11 assists for 17 points . Four players are tied for second in points with 10: Will Smith, Michael Misa, Ivar Stenberg and Jacob Trouba. Goaltender Yaroslav Askarov is 4-7-0 with an .888 save percentage (SV%) and 3.29 goals against average (GAA) in 11 games played.

Speaking to David Pagnotta on DFO Insider , Dan Milstein of Gold Star Hockey confirmed that Evander Kane would sign with a KHL organization and that a formal announcement should be expected in the next few days. Because of his age and poor play during last season with the Vancouver Canucks, Milstein’s announcement strongly suggests that Kane won’t return to the NHL. Although there were plenty of ups and downs, few players get to enjoy a 16-year career like Kane did. That career began on June 26, 2009, when the Atlanta Thrashers selected Kane with the fourth overall pick in the 2009 NHL Draft. He immediately jumped to the NHL, scoring 14 goals and 26 points in 66 games, good for a ninth-place finish in Calder Trophy voting. Kane spent one more season with the Thrashers and remained with the team when they relocated, becoming the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets. His first season in Winnipeg is arguably his career-best campaign. The Vancouver, BC, native finished second on the team in scoring behind Blake Wheeler , registering 30 goals and 57 points in 74 games with a +11 rating. A few weeks before the 2012-13 campaign was supposed to start, the Jets signed Kane to a six-year, $31.5MM ($5.25MM AAV) extension. items.body: OneCourt’s technology allows fans to feel each play as it happens The NHL and Ticketmaster are teaming to bring complimentary OneCourt haptic tablets to blind and low-vision fans at all the League’s tentpole events in North America this season. OneCourt’s broadcast technology converts real-time game data into vibrations that allows fans to feel each play as it happens. Implementation of the program began with the 2026 Tim Horton’s NHL Heritage Classic between the Winnipeg Jets and Montreal Canadiens at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg, Manitoba on Oct. 25. It will continue at the Discover NHL Winter Classic between the Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, Utah on Dec. 31, the 2027 Honda NHL All-Star Weekend at UBS Arena, home of the New York Islanders, on Feb. 5-6, and the 2027 Navy Federal Credit Union NHL Stadium Series between the Dallas Stars and Vegas Golden Knights at AT&T Stadium, home of the Dallas Cowboys, on Feb. 20. In addition, the Avalanche, Washington Capitals, Chicago Blackhawks and Detroit Red Wings will be the first NHL teams to offer OneCourt tablets to fans at their home games. "This partnership with the National Hockey League is a milestone achievement for accessibility in live sports," Kurt Schwartzkopf, head of sports at Ticketmaster, said. "Ticketmaster is proud to support our NHL partners in bringing this experience to life and advance our mission to make live events inclusive and accessible to every fan.” The NHL has been a leader in sports accessibility as the only major professional sports league to produce live game broadcasts in American Sign Language (ASL) through “NHL in ASL.” Now the League is joining Ticketmaster’s ongoing efforts to enhance the game-day experience for blind and low-vision fans.

items.body: Liam Pue first put on skates and hit the ice at age two at home in Langley, B.C., in the arms of his father, Jason. Liam was a quick learner, so much so that his mom, Kristin, joked to her husband, "Geez, he almost skates better than he walks." Because of that early ability, and with Liam wanting to follow his brother Landon —three years older — into hockey, his parents looked for programs to help their youngest son improve his skills. There was one problem, though. "We went through a season where he's skating pretty well for his age, but there's no programs," Jason recalled this week. "I started signing him up for programs, but I lied about his age." "I remember one day my wife had taken him to a skate and there was kind of a new coach on the ice working with Liam," Jason said. "After the skate, this coach came up to the parent-viewing area, and he opened the door, and he said, 'Whose kid is wearing the Datsyuk jersey?' My wife just buried her head cause she was like, 'Oh my goodness, he knows we lied about his age.' Finally, she kind of waved, and he just came up, and he said, 'Your kid is awesome.'" That first meeting with coach Curtis Fraser, a former pro player and cousin of ex-NHLer Colin Fraser, turned out to be the start of a long, productive partnership. For years, Liam Pue played under Fraser up an age group or two with a familiar group of teammates. Pue continued working with Fraser at the Langley Hockey Academy as a teenager. That development path, with much of it outside the Hockey Canada umbrella, turned out to be a perfect fit for Pue. The 16-year-old winger is in the midst of a fantastic first full season in the WHL with the Regina Pats and is considered a top candidate for the 2028 NHL Draft, alongside fellow fast riser and Pats teammate Maddox Schultz.

Seattle bounced back after a 6-2 loss against Calgary on Oct. 30. The loss is the Flames’ first in overtime this season. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Seattle’s Berkly Catton preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to his goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 5:13 (14:47 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Vilmanis has first two-goal game, Panthers top Blackhawks to cap homestand
items.summary: Sandis Vilmanis had the first two-goal game of his career, Sam Reinhart provided a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-3 on Wednesday night to wrap up a three-game homestand.
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Sandis Vilmanis had the first two-goal game of his career, Sam Reinhart provided a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-3 on Wednesday night to wrap up a three-game homestand. Seth Jones scored against his former team and Carter Verhaeghe had a goal and an assist for the Panthers, who are 4-1-0 in their last five games and 7-3-0 in their past 10. Vilmanis added two assists to finish with four points. Florida improved to 9-0-1 when allowing three goals or fewer this season. Reinhart's goal was an empty-netter to seal the win with 1:27 left. Frank Nazar had two third-period goals and Roman Kantserov also scored for Chicago. Ethan Del Mastro got two assists — his first points of the season, and the first multi-point game of his career. Connor Bedard had two assists. The Blackhawks are 1-6-1 in their last eight games. They gave up the final five goals in a 5-2 home loss to Colorado on Monday, then got down 3-0 in Florida before Kantserov got Chicago on the board. By then, the Panthers were already in full control. Vilmanis scored 4:43 into the game, and Verhaeghe’s power-play goal was assisted by Brady Tkachuk and Matthew Tkachuk at 12:29 of the first. Jones beat former Florida goalie Spencer Knight — they were traded for one another in the deal that sent Jones to the Panthers — for a 3-0 lead in the second. Nazar beat Panthers goalie Jacob Markström on a short-handed breakaway to cut Florida’s lead midway through the third. Vilmanis struck again with 8:59 left, restoring the two-goal edge. Nazar got his second of the game with 3:51 left, but Reinhart scored his ninth of the season to all but end the Blackhawks' comeback hopes.

Fabian Zetterlund and Tim Stutzle assisted on the go-ahead goal as Ottawa and Amadio capitalized on a 3-on-2 break. Shane Pinto also scored for the Senators, tying the game at 1 at 11:33 of the second period. Peyton Krebs scored at the 14-minute mark of the first to give the Sabres the lead. Tage Thompson and Zach Benson assisted on Krebs' first goal of the season. Samuel Ersson made 24 saves in the win for the Senators, who entered the game having lost three of their last four games, including a 6-3 setback against Anaheim on Sunday. Colten Ellis had 28 saves for the Sabres, who had their three-game win streak halted. Senators: Host the Utah Mammoth on Saturday in the opener of a three-game homestand. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Fans of the Montreal Canadiens have finally received some clarity regarding an injury to one of their top players. On Wednesday’s episode of DFO Insider with Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta, Dan Milstein, the agent of Canadiens winger Ivan Demidov, revealed that Demidov suffered a fractured ankle during the preseason. Demidov, 20, has been out since early October with what was classified as a lower-body injury. Despite sustaining the injury in the preseason, the Russian national was active to start the regular season, putting up a goal and an assist in two games before initially getting ruled out for two to four weeks. Now in early November, we’re at the tail end of that time frame, but Milstein suggested that Demidov is still weeks away from returning. “Ivan Demidov is getting ready. Probably a few more weeks or so, we’ll see him back in the lineup,” Milstein said. “Unfortunately, he had a fractured ankle in the preseason. It was bothering him but he continued playing for the two games. I saw him after the first game of the season in Toronto, he walked up to me and said ‘Hey, something is bothering (me), something is not right.’ Then he goes out, plays the second game and we did an MRI. Hopefully Ivan will be back on the ice in a very short while and he’ll help the Montreal Canadiens start winning some games.” Demidov is coming off a sterling rookie season, in which he notched 19 goals and 43 assists for 62 points in all 82 regular season games, finishing second in voting for the Calder Trophy. items.summary: Doug Armstrong, Brad Treliving, and Bruce Cassidy round out Hockey Canada’s new National Teams Advisory Group.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Some prominent names are coming together to form an advisory group for Hockey Canada. On Wednesday, Hockey Canada announced that Steve Yzerman, Shane Doan, Doug Armstrong, Brad Treliving, and Bruce Cassidy will make up a new National Teams Advisory Group. According to a press release issued by Hockey Canada, the group will “provide mentorship, leadership and hockey acumen to the organization’s men’s, women’s and para hockey teams, and hockey operations department.” Cassidy had already been hired by Hockey Canada in September as a special advisor to Daniele Sauvageau, the general manager of the national women’s team. The Ottawa native was a head coach in the NHL for parts of nine seasons with the Boston Bruins and Vegas Golden Knights , winning a Stanley Cup with Vegas in 2023. He also served as an assistant coach for the Canadian men’s national team at the 4 Nations Face-Off in 2025 and the Winter Olympics in 2026. Yzerman is currently a senior advisor for the Detroit Red Wings after stepping down as the team’s general manager in July. The Cranbrook, B.C. native served as Detroit’s general manager for seven seasons, and previously served as the Tampa Bay Lightning ‘s general manager for eight seasons. He was also the general manager for the Canadian men’s national team at the 2010 and 2014 Winter Olympics, and the 2007, 2008, and 2013 IIHF World Championships. items.summary: The Jets entered Tuesday’s game against the Canadiens at an all-time low. But then the they pulled out a miracle, which could be just the kind of confidence boost the team needed.
items.body: WINNIPEG — The Winnipeg Jets have stopped the bleeding — for now. The Jets pulled off the impossible on Tuesday, scoring four goals over a span of just two minutes and six seconds before defenceman Dylan Samberg scored in overtime to complete a thrilling 5-4 comeback victory over the Montreal Canadiens at the Bell Centre. They were coming off arguably the worst defeat in Jets' 2.0 history, falling 7-0 to the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. Winnipeg looked listless, appearing to quit on itself in what was a ninth consecutive loss. A loss to the Canadiens would have been a 10th straight defeat, giving the Jets two separate double-digit losing skids in the same calendar year after Winnipeg lost 11 consecutive games during the 2025-26 campaign. Instead, the Jets found some last-minute Montreal magic to break the slide, erupting from the bench in pure joy and a large dose of relief. "That felt like a playoff win in there," Jets head coach Scott Arniel said after the game. "I'm so happy for them, and they're so happy for each other. We've been talking about it for the last stretch here, about staying together as a group. We lose together, we win together, but we just stay together. I just felt tonight, you could see it and we went after them." When it comes to the league's standings, not much. While it was a thrilling win, it still counts the same as any other victory, with the Jets (5-8-3) still sitting three games below a modest .500 record. Winnipeg is currently seventh place in the Central Division, behind only the rebuilding Chicago Blackhawks. items.title: Maple Leafs’ Bobrovsky talks goalie interference: ‘There’s lots of grey area’
items.summary: The Mammoth scored a questionable goal on Sergei Bobrovsky in Tuesday’s Maple Leafs loss. The veteran goaltender discussed the confusion surrounding goaltender interference in the NHL.
items.body: TORONTO — After a night’s sleep to process the sequence of events, Sergei Bobrovsky still has questions about the goal that was scored on him Tuesday evening, moments after Utah Mammoth forward Barrett Hayton collided with the netminder. The Maple Leafs came up just short in a narrow loss to Utah Tuesday at Scotiabank Arena, the Mammoth potting a late power-play goal to quell a Toronto comeback effort. But it was the visitors’ second goal, midway through the tilt, that has the Maple Leafs faithful still up in arms. The play came three minutes after Jack Roslovic had earned a tying goal for the home side. Late in the second period, Bobrovsky came up with a save that saw the puck deflected back out to the point — as Utah's Andrew Peeke wound up to put another attempt on the cage, Hayton cut across the net front, clipped Bobrovsky’s right skate and fell over the goaltender’s leg as the puck flew past them both and into the twine. items.body: Register Login Assessing The Winnipeg Jets Roster Options By Josh Cybulski | at November 4, 2026 3:45 pm Despite an insane come-from-behind win last night, the Winnipeg Jets are a mess right now, sitting at 5-8-3 and on the verge of watching their season slip away before it even started. The team is mired in a run of bad hockey that is putting pressure on ownership to make changes, and it feels like the Jets are approaching a crossroads that could define the franchise. Some folks still hope the team can turn things around this year, and there’s plenty of time left in the season to do so. But other folks are wondering whether a retool or a rebuild should be in order. The latter could prove difficult, given the big-money long-term deals the Jets have with some of their veterans, as well as a fanbase that might not turn up in droves to watch a rebuilding team. The question about the current roster isn’t exactly cut-and-dried. After all, this is a team that, just two years ago, won the Presidents’ Trophy and still has much of that team’s talent in the current lineup. But Nikolaj Ehlers and Connor Hellebuyck , two centerpieces of that team, are gone, and some might wonder whether this team has the roster and organizational depth to push for another playoff spot after missing the postseason last year. The Jets probably don’t need a rebuild and likely can’t pull one off, but most pundits would say they need to rethink their current roster construction. items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Jakob Chychrun found himself in a spot during Tuesday night’s game between the Washington Capitals and the Dallas Stars at Capital One Arena. During the first period of Washington’s eventual 6-5 loss, Chychrun went awkwardly into the boards behind the Capitals’ net while making a puck recovery on a power play. The feet-first collision knocked the skate blade out of his right skate and left him immobile right in front of goaltender Logan Thompson . The high-scoring defenseman immediately shouted for help from his teammates and he got it from captain Alex Ovechkin , who propelled Chychrun toward Washington’s bench with a couple of spears to the fallen defender’s rear end. No, that isn’t running back Saquon Barkley executing the Philadelphia Eagles’ famous Tush Push by shoving quarterback Jalen Hurts over the pile to earn a first down; it’s the greatest goal scorer in the history of the NHL jabbing his good pal in the rump to help save the remaining time on Washington’s power play. With Ovechkin’s assistance, the near-helpless Chychrun could quickly get off the ice for repairs, replaced by Cole Hutson with nearly 90 seconds remaining on the man advantage. Ovechkin has recorded plenty of assists during his career, still just two shy of overtaking Nicklas Backstrom for Washington’s all-time franchise lead, but he won’t see his name on the scoresheet for this one. Despite the quicker-than-usual end to his power-play shift and time on the bench to get a new blade installed, Chychrun still led all skaters in the game with 26:50 of ice time. He later scored his second goal of the season on another power-play and notched his ninth assist on Ryan Leonard ‘s late third-period goal.

items.body: TORONTO — William Nylander is a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma smothered in paradoxical stats. The Toronto Maple Leafs superstar is producing at a rate that puts him well within striking distance of his first 50-goal, 100-point campaign. And yet, the winger’s under-the-hood metrics are troubling at even-strength. The check engine light is blaring orange. Despite starting 62.7 per cent of his shifts in the offensive zone, the second highest of his career, the Leafs are generating just 46.2 per cent of shot attempts when he’s on the ice. His faceoff wins have sunk to a career-low 29.4 per cent. He’s a minus-1 on a team with a plus-6 goal differential, and he’s largely avoided the toughest defensive matchups, which get assigned to Auston Matthews . 32 Thoughts: The Podcast Hockey fans already know the name, but this is not the blog. Among all Leafs skaters this season, Nylander rates 20th in expected goals percentage (40.3) 5-on-5. items.summary: It’s been less than a week since Kucherov requested a trade from the Lightning.
items.body: On Wednesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton are joined by The Fourth Period’s David Pagnotta to discuss the Kucherov rumors and if the Lightning would be better off keeping the three-time Art Ross Trophy winner for the rest of the season. Tyler Yaremchuk : How confident are you that Kucherov will be with a different club by the trade deadline? David Pagnotta : A lot of it depends on Tampa’s performance. If things go south, if guys get injured, if they’re on the outside of the playoffs looking in and it’s looking bleak, then you look at trading him. If you’re going to be this contender and you look at all the odds, I mean, they’re No. 4 or 5 in terms of Stanley Cup favorites … what would you trade him for? Go get another Stanley Cup and if he walks, he walks. But at least you won a Stanley Cup out of it, or at least you made the attempt. I just don’t see a scenario where it makes sense for the Lightning to do it. They’re in the thick of things, so trading Kucherov makes no sense. If you’re a Cup contender, you’re not giving up significant assets on your current roster because you want to build off it. It’s similar to the Minnesota Wild’s thinking with Dylan Larkin. “I’ll give you some assets to make the money work, but I’m not giving you my top guys because it’s a lateral move. It doesn’t make sense.” With Kucherov, if any team is a Cup contender, it’s going to be primarily a futures-driven deal because you want to chase a Cup. items.title: Canadiens pick up the pieces after ’embarrassing, unacceptable’ collapse against Jets
items.body: The Montreal Canadiens were still digesting their epic, history-making collapse a little more than 12 hours later. In a stunning turnaround that made headlines across North America — Fox News called it a "choke job almost too shocking to believe" — the Canadiens surrendered a four-goal lead with 2:39 remaining in regulation and lost 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night. "I don't know, it's hard right now," veteran centre Jake Evans said after practice Wednesday morning. "I think we're all still swallowing it up." It was the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history, smashing the previous mark by more than four minutes. Teams had a record of 0-10,299-0 when facing a deficit of at least four goals entering the final three minutes of regulation before Tuesday. The Jets scored four goals in 126 seconds to erase the lead. You have to go back to Jan. 21, 1919, when Montreal gave up four goals in 100 seconds against the Toronto Arenas, to find a faster stretch of four goals against in Canadiens history. "It's hard to explain," said head coach Martin St. Louis, whose playing career spanned 1,134 NHL games. "I've never been part of something like that." St. Louis is known for his optimistic, inspirational approach to coaching. He was relatively calm in his post-game news conference Tuesday but made clear a day later he wasn’t glossing over the jaw-dropping defeat as the Canadiens (9-3-3) prepare to host the Utah Mammoth on Thursday. "The league doesn't care what we just went through, so we just got to own it," St. Louis said. "It was embarrassing, unacceptable. But you hope that we move on, we fix it, and we keep going. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Russell LaBounty-Imagn Images A couple of Columbus Blue Jackets players have hit the waiver wire. On Wednesday, the Blue Jackets placed forward Danton Heinen and defenseman Emil Andrae on waivers. Both players are available to be claimed by any of the other 31 NHL teams. If they clear waivers, they’ll be eligible to be assigned to the Cleveland Monsters of the American Hockey League (AHL). Heinen, 31, has gone scoreless in 10 games played for Columbus this season. The Blue Jackets acquired him , along with second- and third-round draft picks, from the Pittsburgh Penguins in December of last season in exchange for forward Egor Chinakhov. In 33 games for the Blue Jackets last season following the trade, he had five goals and five assists for 10 points. Selected by the Boston Bruins in the fourth round of the 2014 NHL Entry Draft, the Langley, British Columbia native has played for five different franchises over 11 NHL seasons. His career-best campaign came in his first full-time NHL season with Boston in 2017-18, when he registered 16 goals and 31 assists for 47 points in 77 games. Heinen is currently on a one-year, $1 million deal with Columbus. Andrae, 24, has no goals and two assists in five games for the Blue Jackets this season, while averaging about 10 and a half minutes of ice time. Columbus acquired him just before the season as part of the deal that sent forward Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs and forward Matthew Knies to the Blue Jackets. He is in the first season of a two-year, $3.1 million contract . The Swedish national was acquired by Toronto over the offseason in the deal that sent goaltender Joseph Woll to the Philadephia Flyers . items.title: Maple Leafs’ Tavares could return Saturday, Roslovic misses practice
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs ' top six could get a massive boost on Saturday. Head coach Jim Hiller is hoping to see John Tavares back in the lineup against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday Night Hockey on Sportsnet. Tavares completed his first practice with the team on Wednesday since suffering a lower-body injury three weeks ago. He was in a non-contact red jersey. Hiller said Tavares had a "really good practice," and his next step will be another practice on Friday before seeing if he can play on Saturday. The 36-year-old also participated in a team skate on Tuesday, and his status was updated to day-to-day. Tavares had two goals and five assists in seven games before his injury. Elsewhere, Jack Roslovic was absent from practice due to maintenance, per the Maple Leafs. Roslovic suffered an undisclosed injury near the end of Tuesday's loss to the Utah Mammoth. Following the game, Hiller said something was going on, but he didn't think it was too serious. The winger scored twice on Tuesday to bring his season totals to eight goals and 10 assists in 17 games.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The WHL is heading back to Chilliwack, bringing top-level junior hockey to the British Columbia city for the first time since 2011, when the Chilliwack Bruins moved to the provincial capital to become the Victoria Royals. On Wednesday, the WHL announced that the Fraser Valley municipality had been granted expansion rights to the league’s 24th team, with plans to drop the puck in the 2027-28 season. The new hockey club will be led by an ownership group of Jeremy Colliton, Brett Motherwell, Mason Raymond, Mario Amantea, and Patrick Lathrop. While the team name is still undecided, the Bruins name has a long history in Chilliwack, dating back to the BC Junior Hockey League’s 1970-71 season. Since then, junior hockey in the city has been known by monikers including the Colts, the Eagles, and most recently, the Chiefs, a current team in the BCHL. The new franchise will play out of the Chilliwack Coliseum, a 5,000-seat multi-purpose arena that currently hosts the BCHL’s Chiefs. items.title: Sirens sign Emma Peschel to three-year contract
items.summary: New York selected the Ohio State standout with the seventh-overall pick in this year’s PWHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL One of the top young rearguards in women’s hockey has inked her first professional contract. On Wednesday, the New York Sirens signed defender Emma Peschel to a three-year contract, which will carry through the 2028-29 season. Peschel was one of the top blueliners of the 2026 PWHL Draft class . The Sirens selected her seventh overall in Detroit this past June, the third defender taken in the event, after Laila Edwards, selected fourth overall by the expansion team in San Jose , and Nelli Laitinen, who went sixth overall to Hamilton. Peschel enters the PWHL following a standout career at Ohio State University. There, she became not only one of the best defensive players in all of college hockey, but she developed into one of the top two-way players at her position. Her efforts made the Buckeyes one of the top teams not just in the WCHA, but in the NCAA. As a sophomore, she was a young but crucial piece to Ohio State’s run to the national championship, the program’s second national title. In her four years as a Buckeye, Peschel appeared in 151 games, scoring 31 goals and 77 assists for 108 points. As a senior, she was a First-Team All-American, one year removed from when she was a Second-Team All-American as a junior. The Edina, Minn. native’s play has also earned her some international credibility. After taking home a silver medal at the 2022 IIHF Under-18 Women’s World Championship, she earned a spot on the U.S. National Team roster for the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship, set to begin on Friday. With the signing, the Sirens now have 20 players under contract for the 2026-27 season, giving them four more spots to fill before the new campaign. items.title: Opinion: Canada And Other Nations Deserve Credit For Drawing A Line On Russian IIHF Participation
items.summary: The hockey world was shaken by a CAS ruling that has allowed Russian teams to return to play in IIHF tournaments. But there's a growing boycott of tournaments with Russian participation, and the countries who do so will be on the right side of history.
items.body: Thomas Lovelock via USA Today Sports Thomas Lovelock via USA Today Sports Opinion: Canada And Other Nations Deserve Credit For Drawing A Line On Russian IIHF Participation Adam Proteau Partner Nov 4, 2026 7:07 PM Published Nov 4, 2026 7:07 PM The hockey world was shaken by a CAS ruling that has allowed Russian teams to return to play in IIHF tournaments. But there's a growing boycott of tournaments with Russian participation, and the countries who do so will be on the right side of history. We're living in a complicated world where politics increasingly finds its way into our everyday lives. The hockey world is no exception. The most recent example of this is the impact of Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine. After the baffling decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) that has forced the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) to reinstate Russian teams to its tournaments, seven countries — Sweden, Finland, Czechia, Norway, Latvia and Denmark — have spoken out against the decision and have agreed to actively boycott any events with Russian participation. Whether or not you agree with that decision, those seven nations deserve credit for taking a stance against Russia. More Videos Meanwhile, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday that athletes representing Russia in all sports would not be permitted to play on Canadian soil as the war against Ukraine continues. That includes the world junior hockey championship, which begins next month in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. None of them had to do anything. They could have simply shrugged their shoulders and announced to the world that they had no choice but to abide by the CAS's decision and allowed Russia back into international competition. items.title: How teams and star players would benefit from shorter-term contracts
items.summary: In the flat cap era, every team was chasing contract efficiencies to ice the best rosters. But Justin Bourne writes now that the cap is rising so much, both teams and players should reconsider how they think about contract term.
items.body: Dylan Larkin asked for a trade in year four of an eight-year deal. Connor Hellebuyck asked for a trade in year three of a seven-year deal. Brady Tkachuk made it to year six of his before he wanted out, which was granted before year seven began. All of these players wielded no-trade clauses that hampered any potential return their teams could get, which was a bad deal for the fans twice — they lost a star, and recouped little for him. For these and other elite NHLers, I understand the desire to sign for eight years the second you have a team willing to give it to you. But when it came to these truly top-end guys, the “give me the max dollars and length” always felt like contracts written with crayons rather than calligraphy. Sure you're able to get a big long-term deal, but if you're a proven top-end player in the NHL, wouldn't you want to maintain some flexibility on where you play? The way Auston Matthews has done his contracts has always made sense to me. He's signed five- and four-year contracts after his entry-level deal with the Leafs and has made good money, but never sought out maximum length. Five years is a big commitment to a city, isn’t it? And really, who among us knows what our priorities will be in five years? “I’m happy to re-up when we get there, let’s just re-assess if everyone’s happy” is a thought process I’ve never wavered in defending. If you have priorities beyond money (as most of us do), it might be wise to build those concerns into your contract. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kyle Ross-Imagn Images Following Tuesday night’s loss to the Minnesota Wild , the Philadelphia Flyers fell to a record of 4-9-4 on the season. It goes without saying that it has been a campaign full of disappointments to this point, but one of the few bright spots has been the play of winger Matvei Michkov. Michkov, who turns 22 next month, has 10 goals and three assists through 17 games this season. Michkov is in the final year of his entry-level contract, and his hot start has many wondering what his next deal will look like. Speaking with sources earlier this week, Daily Faceoff was told there have been no discussions to this point with Michkov’s camp on what the player’s next deal could look like. That being said, it is never too early to start projecting it. Historically, the Flyers have liked to bridge their younger players following their ELCs. According to sources, while a bridge isn’t off the table for Michkov, there does seem to be an appetite to explore several options as to what his next contract will ultimately be. items.title: Voters reject proposed taxes tied to planned new arena for Dallas Stars
items.summary: Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL’s Stars.
items.body: PLANO, Texas — Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL's Stars. Unofficial results from Tuesday's vote in the city of Plano showed 54.6 per cent of the more than 102,000 votes cast were against the single ballot proposal to authorize taxes on tickets, parking, car rentals, hotel rooms and the professional teams that would use the arena. Those taxes were to help the city pay off up to $700 million in bonds it has committed to the proposed $3 billion mixed-use development that would include the new arena. The vote was about the proposed taxes, and not whether the $1-billion arena could be built as part of a large-scale redevelopment project of The Shops at Willow Bend, where the last enclosed mall built in Texas is being demolished. It could include sports, entertainment, retail, dining and public gathering spaces. “The proposed redevelopment at The Shops at Willow Bend remains an important opportunity for our community," Plano Mayor John Muns said in a statement. “We are committed to thoughtful reinvestment and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars as we consider what comes next.” The hockey-specific arena would be owned by the city, with the Stars intending to lease it for 30 years. Stars officials hope to move in 2031 about 20 miles north of the downtown American Airlines Center, which they have shared with the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks since it opened in 2001. The leases at the AAC for both teams expire in 2031, and the Mavericks have plans for a similar project of their own away from downtown, about 10 miles north on the former site of a Dallas mall.

items.body: NEWARK, N.J. -- Ryan Nugent-Hopkins felt the significance of his next game and the milestone it represents for the Edmonton Oilers when he saw his teammates Tuesday morning. There they were, all wearing T-shirts that depicted the Oilers forward with a mullet, smoking a cigarette, wearing a short-sleeved camo shirt, and with a tattoo on his arm. The 32-year-old forward, selected by Edmonton with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft, passed Kevin Lowe, who played 1,037 games during his 15 seasons with the Oilers. They are the two to have played at least 1,000 games for Edmonton. "I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team," Nugent-Hopkins said Tuesday. "It really is a testament to a lot of these guys in this room, and not just the players but the staff, the trainers that have been here for my entire career." After showing him the T-shirts, the Oilers played him a video celebrating his career. "I feel the love," Nugent-Hopkins said. "Having a video that they shared with me was definitely special. To have experienced a lot of these games with a few of the guys in here, it's pretty special. I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team." items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Following a tumultuous exit from Manitoba, former Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is explaining why he wanted out of town. On his personal Instagram, Hellebuyck wrote a letter to Jets fans, giving the reasons why he requested a trade from the only franchise he’d ever known. Hellebuyck stated that asking to be dealt by the Jets wasn’t an easy decision, but he had his reasons. “I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career,” Hellebuyck wrote. “I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision. There were several considerations that went into my decision, including some very challenging circumstances involving my family. Korpisalo, 32, has been recovering from a lower-body injury and foot infection suffered at the beginning of the season. The Wolf Pack later confirmed the transaction. Because Korpisalo is on the injured reserve, not the long-term injured reserve, the conditioning loan’s duration is governed by Section 13.8 of the NHL’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, not Section 13.9. items.title: Major sponsors threatening to pull out of IIHF tournaments if Russia is allowed back in
items.summary: Some of the brands that have become synonymous with international hockey might back out.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources As if the countries threatening to boycott International Ice Hockey Federation tournaments weren’t enough, big-name sponsors might follow suit following a recent court ruling. On Wednesday, several reports came out that several sponsors that have been associated with the IIHF – AJ Produkter, Skoda and Strauss – have made statements regarding the potential return of the Russian Ice Hockey Federation to IIHF events.
